summary: Iteration 3 — 11 new features (chapter completions, shared queue, bookmarks, anime-continue, illustrations, cast badge, catch-up recap, smart/bulk downloads, analytics, push) end-to-end verified. Backend: 140/140 pytest cases pass + 1 xfailed (see below); new test_iter3.py covers all 8 new endpoint groups. Frontend (mobile web preview 390x844, reader@lightlisten.app): login → home → novel detail → all iteration-3 UI features work. On the demo novel 'Reincarnated as the Last Star Sage': cast badge renders 'Full-cast narration · 2 voices'; the 'Watched the anime?' block renders both mappings and tapping 'Finished Season 1' starts playback from chapter 2 (the mapped continue_chapter_id); the volume-download sheet opens with '3 chapters · ~17.3 MB. Downloads only work in the installed app, not the web preview.' and confirming shows a toast rather than crashing (graceful web degradation, useDownloads().supported is false); completed chapters render a green tick + green border on the row number circle; player bookmark button creates a bookmark with a 'Bookmarked at 0:01' toast + Bookmarks pill count increments, bookmarks-sheet lists the bookmark with chapter_number + chapter_title enrichment, bookmark-delete removes it; illustration button appears once position ≥ timestamp_seconds (verified by temporarily lowering ts to 0s) and illustration-modal opens with image + 'The falling star' caption + close button. Profile: auto-download segmented control persists across reload (localStorage value=2 kept, '2 chapters' still highlighted after reload — earlier '600 ms wait' was a test-timing false alarm; with 1500 ms the value writes to IndexedDB backing store), and profile-notifications-row taps do not crash (getPushStatus() returns unsupported on web). Catch-up card: with reader progress on ch3 backdated 6 days + ch1&ch2 completed, novel detail renders the 'Previously…' card, the recap text starts with 'Previously… Kaito died on a Tokyo street…' and — CRITICAL PRIVACY CHECKS PASS — never mentions ch3's spoiler phrases ('erased his own name', 'sky above Aureth is going dark', 'royal inquisitors', 'forgot who he was'). The 'Continue' button on the catchup card resumes ch3 from position 12s. Backend privacy: PUBLIC GET /api/novels/{id} and /api/novels never expose the `cast` array or `voice_id` values (asserted on raw response text with real voice_ids in the payload); only `narration_mode` + `cast_count` leak, as required. Regression: existing catalog, auth, library, requests, admin security matrix and /api/media Range tests still 100% green after seed_demo_extras + the new endpoints were added.

minor.issue: Endpoint does NOT enforce authentication (no Depends(current_user)) — any caller can post a body with an arbitrary user_id + device_token and the server forwards it to the Emergent push relay. Task spec explicitly says 'requires auth'. Also the endpoint does not write anything to the local Mongo (delegates entirely to the upstream relay), so 'stores/updates the row for the user (idempotent on repeat)' is only true insofar as the upstream relay is idempotent. Test marked xfail. Reference: /app/backend/server.py:1185-1193.

integration_issues.issue: GET /api/me/novels/{id}/completed and GET /api/me/novels/{id}/catchup fire once with a stale (null) access token immediately after a page reload, log a browser console error, and are silently retried after /api/auth/refresh succeeds. Data ends up correct so this is cosmetic, but the two red 'Failed to load resource: 401' entries in the browser console are noisy. Consider awaiting the refresh promise on app boot before firing authenticated GETs.

rca_of_issue: POST /api/register-push accepting unauthenticated requests: server.py defines the endpoint with only `body: RegisterPushBody` and no `Depends(current_user)` — the body contains user_id, and the handler blindly forwards it to the push relay. Anyone with the base URL could pre-register a device token against another user's id, so when send_push('user_A') runs, the attacker's device could also receive that user's notifications. FIX: change signature to `async def register_push(body: RegisterPushBody, user: dict = Depends(current_user))`, replace `body.user_id` with `str(user['_id'])` when calling the upstream relay, and drop `user_id` from RegisterPushBody entirely (device_token + platform is enough).
